adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via unsanitized imported HTML: cook_method raw_html bypasses the Markdown/Sanitize pipeline, and remote/RSS content with scripts is rendered with raw in embed view

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `cook_method` option where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`, using content sourced from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or remote HTML (`Readability::Document` output). In the embed view, the post body is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for `raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw` (as asserted in the spec). There is no sanitization step in `TopicEmbed.import` for RSS content, so a feed containing `<script>`/event handlers/etc. would be stored and then rendered as HTML, constituting stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Protocol-relative URLs (starting with //) are incorrectly matched by href.start_with?('/') in absolutize_urls, producing broken URLs

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, any href/src that starts with '/' is treated as a relative-path URL and rewritten as "#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}". A protocol-relative URL like "//cdn.example.com/a.js" also starts with '/', so it will be rewritten to something like "http://<original-host>/cdn.example.com/a.js", which is incorrect/broken because "//..." is already an absolute (scheme-relative) URL and should not be prefixed with the page host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import crashes with NoMethodError when embed.post is nil because there is no dependent-destroy/cleanup of topic_embeds rows

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content changed, calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and later `revisor.revise!`. If `embed.post` is `nil` (e.g., the referenced post was deleted, since the migration adds `post_id` without a foreign key and there is no `dependent: :destroy`/cleanup association shown), this will crash (likely via NoMethodError inside `PostRevisor` when it assumes `@post` is a Post). The diff provides no protection against orphaned `topic_embeds` rows or a nil post association.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed polling failures are silently dropped: PollFeed has retry: false and no error handling, so one bad item aborts the entire poll with no notification

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the scheduled job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and `poll_feed` performs network/parse work (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, and then per-item processing including `i.content.scrub`) with no `rescue` or per-item error handling. Any exception (bad feed, transient network error, malformed item missing `content`, etc.) will raise and abort the whole polling run. With retries disabled, Sidekiq will not retry the job, so the failure can result in that poll run being dropped (aside from logging) and no further items processed in that execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import partially mutates state (contents << ...) before validation and mixes exceptions and nil for error propagation, making failure handling fragile

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the method appends to the caller-provided `contents` string in-place (`contents << "\n<hr>..."`) before any DB write/validation happens. If the subsequent transaction fails (e.g., `PostCreator#create` returns `nil` or `TopicEmbed.create!` raises), the caller’s string has still been mutated, which is a real side effect that can make retry/error handling brittle. Additionally, the method returns `nil` for a malformed URL (`return unless url =~ ...`) but can also fail by raising exceptions (`TopicEmbed.create!`, `revisor.revise!`), mixing `nil`-based and exception-based error signaling in the same API, which is verifiably inconsistent in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view reload loop never terminates on failure, causing unbounded re-enqueuing of RetrieveTopic and synchronous PollFeed runs driven by visitor traffic

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In EmbedController#best, when no existing TopicEmbed is found it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30s with no stop condition, so if retrieval never succeeds (e.g., bad embed_url, remote fetch fails, misconfiguration), the page will reload indefinitely. Each reload re-hits `embed#best` and enqueues another `RetrieveTopic` job (no controller-side throttling). Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` may synchronously run `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, so repeated retrieval attempts (throttled to ~once per 60s per URL via Redis) can still cause repeated feed polling work driven by visitor reloads, and the job queue can grow unbounded from repeated enqueues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_id_for_embed doesn't verify the topic exists, so a stale topic_embeds row causes a 500 on the embed endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` simply plucks `:topic_id` from `topic_embeds` (`pluck(:topic_id).first`) without checking that the referenced `topics` row still exists. `EmbedController#best` treats any non-nil `topic_id` as valid and immediately does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`. Since the migration adds no foreign key constraints and there are no callbacks shown to clean up `topic_embeds` when a topic is deleted, a stale `topic_embeds.topic_id` is possible and would lead to an exception when `TopicView` tries to load the topic (likely resulting in a server error if not handled elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is dead code; the modified-caching concept it implies is computed but never used for conditional fetch

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` computes and memoizes a Redis-style cache key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`), but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key` or uses that key to store/check a last-modified/ETag value. The only logic in `poll_feed` is `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` followed by iterating items. So the finding that `feed_key` is dead/unused and the implied modified-caching is not implemented is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve calls full feed re-parse and TopicEmbed.import for every embed request when feed_polling_enabled, causing material-resource amplification from unauthenticated embed traffic with no limit on feed size or item count

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it unconditionally does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` with no cap on feed size/item count. This path is reachable from unauthenticated embed traffic: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` when no `TopicEmbed` exists, which calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. The only throttle is `retrieved_recently?`, which keys on the full `embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many distinct embed URLs can trigger repeated full feed fetch/parse and imports. Therefore the diff does introduce a verifiable resource-amplification risk (though not literally “every” request; only when the embed isn’t already present / URL not throttled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in poll_feed.rb is computed but never used; no conditional GET (Last-Modified/ETag) check, so the hourly poller unconditionally fetches and parses the whole feed and does an N-query TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:) lookup per item with no batching

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (computes `feed-modified:<sha1>`), but it is never referenced anywhere in the file or diff, so it is dead code and suggests intended caching/Last-Modified handling was not implemented. Also, `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of conditional request headers (ETag/If-Modified-Since), so the feed is fetched and parsed every run. Finally, for each `rss.items.each`, it calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which performs `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` per item, creating an N-per-item query pattern without batching in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote uses open(url).read with no size cap, allowing unbounded download into memory that is then re-parsed twice by Readability and absolutize_urls

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import_remote, the code does `open(url).read` (lib/topic_embed.rb) which reads the entire remote response into memory without any size limit or streaming. That string is then parsed by `Readability::Document.new(...)`, and the resulting `doc.content` is later passed through `absolutize_urls`, which parses it again via `Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(contents)`. This creates a verifiable risk of unbounded memory/CPU consumption if the target URL returns a very large response (even if constrained to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed loading page uses a 30-second fixed-interval reload loop with no cap; failed retrievals leave embeds in a permanent reload loop generating sustained traffic since the Redis throttle only gates the job not the request path

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no cap or fallback. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch fails, invalid content, misconfiguration), the iframe will keep re-requesting `/embed/best` indefinitely, continuously generating HTTP traffic and repeatedly enqueueing jobs. The Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` only limits actual retrieval work (inside the job), not the request/reload loop or the job enqueueing itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Poll feed loop CGI.unescapeHTML/scrubs content for all feed items before any dedup check, doing a full in-memory transform pass where an earlier URL-level existence check could short-circuit

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, each RSS item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. The dedup/update logic (by `embed_url` and `content_sha1`) lives inside `TopicEmbed.import`, which needs the transformed `contents` to compute `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` and decide whether the post changed. A “URL-level existence check” before transforming would incorrectly skip updates when the URL already exists but content has changed. As written, this is at most a performance micro-optimization discussion, not a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :top_topics with force: true in migration 20131223171005 will silently drop existing top_topics table and its data on installs that already ran the original migration, causing unrecoverable data loss

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` does drop-and-recreate the table *when that migration runs*, production installs that already ran this migration will not rerun it because Rails tracks applied migrations in `schema_migrations`. Therefore, it will not “silently drop existing top_topics table and its data on installs that already ran the original migration” during a normal `db:migrate`. The change mainly affects fresh runs from scratch (or environments where the migration is intentionally re-executed via rollback/reset), where dropping is either irrelevant (table doesn’t exist yet) or expected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check using discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is trivially bypassable — empty e.origin passes the check (indexOf('') === 0), and substring matching accepts any origin appearing anywhere in discourseUrl rather than exact origin comparison

embed.html.erb postMessage uses request.referer as targetOrigin, which is nil when iframe is loaded directly, rendering an empty string literal that causes postMessage to throw SyntaxError so the resize message is never delivered
poll_feed.rb calls i.content.scrub on RSS/Atom items, which raises NoMethodError for items without a content element; with retry: false this aborts the entire feed processing persistently each hour
TopicEmbed.import from PollFeed inserts raw RSS item content with cook_method: raw_html, bypassing all sanitization and enabling stored XSS if the feed is compromised or publishes untrusted content

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == ...`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` from the RSS item straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization step. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output that HTML as-is. Therefore, if the feed content contains malicious HTML/JS (or risky attributes), it can be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS. This is directly verifiable from the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor removed the public --category/-c CLI option without deprecation, breaking existing scripts and causing imports to land uncategorized

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` is removed, along with all logic that looked up `Category.where(name: options[:category])` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)`. The new code path calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote/import` do not accept or apply any category setting. This is a verifiable breaking change for existing scripts that used `--category/-c`, and it also eliminates the ability to import Disqus threads into a chosen category (they will fall back to whatever default category behavior is).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb params.require(:embed_url) returns 400 Bad Request while the spec claims 404, making the /embed/best route contract ambiguous; also deleted topics cause TopicView.new to blow up

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `params.require(:embed_url)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when absent, which Rails typically turns into a 400 response unless rescued. However, the spec does not actually assert a 404; it only says "is 404" in the example description and checks `response.should_not be_success`, which is consistent with 400. The claim about deleted topics causing `TopicView.new` to blow up is speculative and not verifiable from the diff (no evidence of deletion behavior/cascades here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb update path assumes embed.post still exists — if the post was deleted (no cascade/FK), PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError, permanently wedging re-import and 500ing the embed endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `post = embed.post` and, if the content sha changed, calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!`. There is no foreign key or `dependent:` option in the diff to ensure `topic_embeds.post_id` always points to an existing post (migration only adds a NOT NULL integer column). If the referenced Post is deleted, `embed.post` will be nil, so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will later dereference `@post` and raise (likely NoMethodError), preventing future re-imports for that embed_url and causing the retrieve job to error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb referer validation compares host strings case-sensitively and the rescue URI::InvalidURIError is placed after the X-Frame-Options assignment, so the header is discarded when the exception raises, making header behavior inconsistent between failure modes

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the `X-Frame-Options` header is only set after both validation `raise`s, so in failure modes it is simply never set because the method aborts; it is not “discarded due to the rescue placement”. The `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` wraps the whole method body and will catch parse errors from `URI(request.referer || '')` regardless of being written after the header assignment. The case-sensitivity concern is also not clearly verifiable from the diff alone (Ruby’s URI handling may normalize hosts), so the proposed finding’s described behavior is not reliably present in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeout on remote fetches using Kernel#open with no options in topic_embed.rb import_remote, poll_feed.rb, and disqus.thor, which blocks indefinitely on slow/hung remote hosts and can pin Sidekiq worker threads

PollFeed job has retry: false and no error handling; a single bad feed item (nil content or title causing NoMethodError) aborts the whole feed and silently skips all subsequent items every hour with no notification

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false` and `poll_feed` has no exception handling around feed parsing or per-item processing. Inside the loop it calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which will raise `NoMethodError` if `i.content` is nil (and similar issues could occur with other missing fields). Any such exception will abort the entire job run before subsequent items are processed, and because retries are disabled Sidekiq will not retry that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic job retries forever (~25 times with backoff) on permanently failing URLs since network errors raise out of the job with no rescue for permanent failures

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which can end up in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, doing `open(url).read` with no rescue. Network/HTTP errors (e.g., `OpenURI::HTTPError`, timeouts) would bubble out and fail the Sidekiq job. Unlike `Jobs::PollFeed`, which explicitly sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, `RetrieveTopic` sets no retry option, so it will use Sidekiq’s default retry behavior (typically ~25 retries with backoff). That means permanently failing URLs can be retried many times rather than being handled as non-retryable failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve runs the entire scheduled feed poll synchronously inline via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}), duplicating the hourly scheduled job's work and blocking the request; should enqueue instead and execute({}) bypasses Sidekiq retry/metrics

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve directly invokes the scheduled job inline: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`. This runs the full feed polling synchronously as part of whatever is calling `TopicRetriever#retrieve` (in this diff, the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` Sidekiq job), rather than being enqueued/run under its own Sidekiq job context. As a result it duplicates work that is already configured to run hourly (Jobs::PollFeed < Jobs::Scheduled) and bypasses Sidekiq job-level behavior for PollFeed itself (its `sidekiq_options retry: false`, scheduled/metrics/middleware separation), while also potentially making the RetrieveTopic job take much longer due to network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`). The finding’s “blocking the request” wording is not strictly accurate for the controller path shown (controller enqueues RetrieveTopic), but the core issue (synchronous inline execution of the scheduled poll) is present and verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle key is set via Redis setnx in retrieved_recently? before perform_retrieve runs, so failed retrieves lock out retry attempts for 60s and the user sees 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, the throttle is applied by `retrieved_recently?` *before* `perform_retrieve` runs. `retrieved_recently?` calls `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and immediately sets a 60s expiry, then returns `false` to allow the first attempt through. If `perform_retrieve` (or deeper calls like `Jobs::PollFeed` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / HTTP fetch) fails or raises, the Redis key remains set for up to 60 seconds, causing subsequent `retrieve` calls (including repeated enqueued jobs from `EmbedController#best` while it renders `loading`) to skip `perform_retrieve` and therefore skip retrying during that window. The "indefinitely" part is overstated (it will retry after the 60s TTL), but the core issue—failed attempts still consume the 60s throttle window—is real and directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController#best raises unhandled when the topic is deleted or TopicView construction fails (best: 5 on topic with no posts, deleted user), rendering a 500 page inside the customer's site instead of the loading view

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns a topic_id, the code unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no rescue/fallback. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed simply plucks `:topic_id` from `topic_embeds` by `embed_url` and does not verify the Topic still exists. If the referenced topic was deleted (or otherwise makes TopicView initialization raise, e.g., RecordNotFound), the exception will bubble and produce a 500 response instead of rendering the 'loading' view (which only happens in the `else` branch when topic_id is nil).

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is dead code — computed but never read or written, so the poll job has no change-detection and re-downloads the full feed hourly, with correctness only saved by SHA1 dedup in TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `feed_key` is defined (computes a Redis key based on the feed URL) but is never referenced anywhere in the diff (no reads/writes to that key). The `poll_feed` method unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items every time it runs; combined with `recurrence { hourly }`, this means the full feed is re-downloaded and re-parsed hourly with no conditional GET/change-detection. Dedup/update behavior is handled later by `TopicEmbed.import` via `embed_url` lookup and `content_sha1` comparison, but that does not prevent the repeated downloading/parsing work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb reload loop depends on discourse_expires_in 1.minute but reloads every 30s with no retry cap or error state if the retrieve job is queued behind a backlog

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally executes `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`, which will reload forever as long as `EmbedController#best` keeps rendering `loading` (i.e., when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` remains nil). There is no max retry count, backoff, or alternate error state. While `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is set in the controller, the reload loop does not actually "depend" on it; however, the core issue of an unbounded 30s reload loop if the background retrieve job is delayed or never succeeds is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage targetOrigin uses request.referer which can be nil/empty in the layout render path, breaking the resize message when referer is absent

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, the `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` enforces a non-blank, valid `request.referer` whose host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (`URI(request.referer || '').host != ...` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess`). If the referer is nil/empty, the request is rejected and the `embed` layout (and its `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`) will not be rendered. Therefore the layout render path should not see a nil/empty referer under normal routing through this controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller tests in embed_controller_spec.rb fully stub TopicRetriever/TopicView and only assert mocks were called; no test that the best view actually renders posts from a real embedded topic or that the loading template renders when no topic exists

adjudication.rationale: The spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb added in this diff does indeed mostly stub/mocks collaborators (TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed, TopicRetriever.new/retrieve, TopicView.new) and does not assert that the controller renders the expected templates (e.g., `render_template('loading')`) or that the rendered `best` view contains post content. However, this is a test coverage/quality critique rather than a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the diff itself. The production code can still be correct even if the tests are shallow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed job logic is never exercised by specs; only guard conditions are tested via stubs, leaving user lookup failure, SimpleRSS parsing, link/id fallback, and TopicEmbed.import delegation untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` with non-trivial behavior (user lookup by `embed_by_username`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, per-item URL fallback to `i.id`, HTML unescape/scrub, and `TopicEmbed.import` call). The accompanying spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts `execute`’s guard conditions and that `poll_feed` is invoked, but it never exercises or asserts any behavior inside `poll_feed` itself. This is directly verifiable from the added code and spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) will raise NoMethodError on feeds where content is nil (common in plain RSS vs Atom)
Post#cook change makes raw_html posts skip Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) with no spec asserting hook filters are intentionally skipped

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Post#cook` so that when `cook_method == :raw_html` it returns `raw` immediately, which necessarily skips `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. However, the proposed finding frames this as a problem because there is “no spec asserting hook filters are intentionally skipped.” Lack of a spec (or an assertion about intent) is not, by itself, a verifiable defect introduced by the diff, and nothing in the diff establishes that `:after_post_cook` must run for `:raw_html` posts. This is therefore speculative/test-coverage commentary rather than a clear correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor skip_validations behavior change has no test; the revisor spec doesn't cover that invalid raw can be saved or that validations still run by default

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which is an intentional behavior change to honor an existing `skip_validations` option (used elsewhere in the diff via `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true)`). The proposed finding is about missing test coverage (no spec added/updated for this), but absence of a test is not a verifiable defect in the code itself, and the new default behavior still runs validations when `skip_validations` is not set. Therefore it does not identify a concrete bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever throttling tests stub retrieved_recently? itself, leaving the Redis setnx/expire throttle logic and no_throttle staff override with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb the “valid host” tests explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false, so they do not exercise the Redis-based throttling logic inside `retrieved_recently?` (setnx/expire) nor the `@opts[:no_throttle]` staff override path. However, this is a test coverage gap rather than a functional defect/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff; the production code can still work correctly even if these branches aren’t directly covered by unit tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing tests for perform_retrieve internals: existing-embed bail-out, PollFeed-first behavior, and fetch_http when embed_by_username user is missing

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` branches (bail out if an embed already exists, run `PollFeed` first when enabled, and `fetch_http` returning early if `embed_by_username` user is missing). The added specs for `TopicRetriever` only cover `invalid_host?` and `retrieved_recently?` gating, not these internal branches. However, this is a test coverage suggestion rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff; the code can still behave correctly without these additional tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb update-path test only checks post.cooked matches new contents; doesn't verify content_sha1 update, dedup skip path, or retention of cook_method raw_html after PostRevisor

adjudication.rationale: The finding is about test completeness, not a defect introduced by the diff. It’s true that the “Supports updating the post” spec only asserts `post.cooked` includes the new contents and does not explicitly assert `content_sha1` is updated, the no-op/dedup path when content is unchanged, or that `cook_method` remains `raw_html` after `PostRevisor`. However, this is an optional strengthening of test coverage rather than a real, verifiable correctness/security bug in the changed code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostCreator cook_method option untested in PostCreator specs, including invalid/nonexistent cook_method values and interaction with existing opts validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds support for passing `:cook_method` through `PostCreator` (`post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method] if @opts[:cook_method].present?`) and adds the `cook_method` enum/column usage in `Post#cook`. However, the proposed finding is about missing/insufficient spec coverage (untested option, invalid values, interaction with existing option validation). This is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: the change does not obviously break behavior, and the diff does not show any existing `PostCreator` spec suite or any opts-validation logic that now conflicts. Lack of tests is a quality concern but not a concrete bug/security/correctness problem evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls port/protocol edge cases untested: https URLs with explicit :443, non-standard ports (:8080), and protocol-relative // hrefs

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, but the only spec coverage added checks simple root-relative URLs like `href='/hello'` and `src='/images/...'`. There are no tests for protocol/port edge cases such as explicit `:443`, non-standard ports (e.g. `:8080`), or protocol-relative URLs (`//example.com/...`). Additionally, the implementation rewrites any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')`, which includes `//...` and would incorrectly transform protocol-relative URLs into paths on the embed host, so the lack of tests leaves a real correctness edge case unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Protocol-relative URLs like src="//cdn.example.com/x.jpg" are mangled by start_with?('/') into http://host//cdn... — a real correctness bug

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both link and image URLs are rewritten whenever `href/src.start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg` also satisfy this condition, and then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips *all* leading slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/x.jpg`. The code then prefixes it with the site host: `"#{prefix}/#{...}"`, resulting in `http://<embed-host>/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, which is incorrect/mangled for protocol-relative URLs. (The finding’s exact example with `//` preserved is slightly off, but the underlying correctness bug is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor import task refactored to TopicEmbed.import_remote with changed behavior (category option removed, remote fetch added) but no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` behavior: it removes the `:category` option and replaces a local `PostCreator` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which fetches and parses remote content. However, the proposed issue is framed as “no test coverage,” and the diff does not introduce or remove any existing tests for this Thor task (there were none shown). Lack of tests for a Rake/Thor task is not, by itself, a verifiable defect/bug/security issue in the code change; it’s a process concern rather than a concrete problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via unsanitized external HTML: remote feed content marked raw_html skips cooking/sanitization and is rendered with raw in embed/best.html.erb

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly adds a `:raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` without running the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from external feed/remote content with `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Jobs::PollFeed`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote` supply HTML sourced from RSS/ATOM (`i.content`) or fetched pages (`Readability::Document#content`). That HTML is then rendered in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` using `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so attacker-controlled HTML (e.g., `<script>` or event handlers) can be stored and executed when the embed is viewed. There is no sanitization step shown in this diff for the raw_html path, so this is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration re-run destroys table: force: true added to already-run create_top_topics migration could drop top_topics table and data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. While already-applied migrations won’t rerun in normal `db:migrate`, if this migration is ever re-executed against a database that already has `top_topics` (e.g., schema_migrations reset, manual rerun/redo without first dropping the DB), it can silently delete the table and its data, whereas the previous version would have raised instead. This is a real destructive behavioral change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weak origin check in postMessage handler: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) substring match allows malicious origins to pass
cook bypasses plugin after_post_cook filters when cook_method is raw_html

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This early return skips the existing call to `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, self, ...)`, so any plugins relying on the `:after_post_cook` hook will not run for raw_html posts (including those created by TopicEmbed.import which sets `cook_method: :raw_html`). This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the diff and can break expected plugin processing/sanitization for those posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Direct synchronous job invocation in TopicRetriever instantiating and executing Jobs::PollFeed, tight coupling to job internals

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, the code does instantiate `Jobs::PollFeed` and call `execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. However, in this diff the primary caller of `TopicRetriever` is `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so this occurs inside a background job, not directly in a controller request. Calling a job class’s `execute` method directly is also not inherently incorrect in this codebase and doesn’t present a clear correctness/bug/security defect by itself; the “tight coupling to job internals” aspect is more of an architectural/style concern than a verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import behavior silently changed: --category option removed and import now re-fetches thread with readability and appends footer, causing functionality regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Disqus Thor task's `--category` option (`method_option :category` is deleted) and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it to `PostCreator`. It also changes the initial topic creation from `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which fetches the remote URL via `open(url).read` and processes it with `ruby-readability`. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` appends an "Imported from" footer to the contents before creating/updating the post. This is a concrete behavior change and removes previously supported functionality (categorizing imports), which is a verifiable regression from the prior CLI behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race on concurrent embed creation: TopicEmbed.create! inside transaction can raise uncaught ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique with unique index on embed_url

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `topic_embeds` has a unique index on `embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does a non-locking read `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, enters a `Topic.transaction` and calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. With concurrent imports of the same URL, both transactions can observe `embed.blank?` and attempt `create!`; the second will violate the unique index and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent), which is not rescued in this method. The earlier `exists?` check in `TopicRetriever` does not eliminate the race (TOCTOU) and other callers (e.g., feed polling) can also hit it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage targetOrigin from client-controlled request.referer: nil referer causes postMessage to throw, and trusting referer is fragile

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code calls parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). The second argument (targetOrigin) must be an origin (scheme+host+port) like "https://eviltrout.com", not a full URL with path/query. request.referer will typically be a full URL (e.g. the embedding page), so this can throw a DOMException / fail to send the resize message in browsers. The proposed point about a nil referer causing this is not accurate because EmbedController#ensure_embeddable rejects missing referers before rendering, but the core issue (using referer as targetOrigin) is a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed item fields assumed present: nil content or title in RSS/Atom items raises NoMethodError aborting entire feed processing with no per-item error isolation

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If an RSS/Atom item has `content` missing (`nil`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, and there is no per-item `rescue`, so the whole feed polling job would abort. Similarly, `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` assumes `i.title` is present, but even without a guaranteed NoMethodError from `title`, missing `content` is a concrete, verifiable crash in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: contents argument mutated as side effect in TopicEmbed#import by appending footer to caller's string

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the method does `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."`, which uses Ruby’s `String#<<` to append in-place. Since `contents` is a caller-provided string, this mutates the argument as a side effect (the caller’s string is permanently modified after the call). This is directly verifiable in the diff and can lead to unexpected behavior if the caller reuses the same string (e.g., double-appended footers or altered data used elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: feed_key method in poll_feed.rb computed but never read or written

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` computes and memoizes a Redis-style key string, but it is never called anywhere within `PollFeed` (the only call sites in the file are `execute` -> `poll_feed`). No other references to `feed_key` appear in the provided diff, so it is verifiably unused/dead code introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: unused require_dependency 'email/sender' in retrieve_topic.rb

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the diff adds `require_dependency 'email/sender'`, but the job implementation only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. There is no reference to `Email::Sender` or any symbol from `email/sender` in this file, so the claim of an unused/extra require is supported by the diff. However, this is a cleanup/performance nit rather than a clear correctness/bug defect introduced by the change (the code will still work with an extra require).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated embed_by_username user lookup in poll_feed.rb and topic_retriever.rb that will drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include two similar user lookups: Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed and TopicRetriever#fetch_http both do `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`. However, this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the change—it's simply duplication. The claim that it "will drift" is speculative and not demonstrably problematic from the diff alone (both use the same SiteSetting and return early if user is blank).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated attribute-rewriting loops in absolutize_urls for a[href] and img[src], also missing protocol-relative URLs

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the rewrite condition is `start_with?('/')` for both `a['href']` and `img['src']`. This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`, which are not actually relative to the article host. The code then prefixes them with `prefix` and strips leading slashes (`href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`), producing an incorrect URL such as `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x.png`. That is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the current logic. The “duplicated loops” part is true (similar code for `a` and `img`) but is more of a refactoring/style observation than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated whitespace-only edit to historical migration migrate_word_counts.rb pollutes blame

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include a whitespace-only change in the historical migration `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` (removing trailing spaces/blank-line whitespace and adding/removing newline markers). However, this is a process/style concern (“pollutes blame”), not a bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the change. Under the given criteria, it’s a style nit rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true, which silently drops an existing topic_embeds table and destroys its data with no rollback path

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which would silently destroy any existing `topic_embeds` data. While migrations typically run once, the flag is unnecessary here for a normal migration and does introduce a data-loss risk if the table exists for any reason (previous partial deploy, manual creation, etc.), and rollback cannot recover the dropped data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true was retroactively added to the already-shipped create_top_topics migration, causing potential data loss on re-run and schema drift between environments

topic_embeds foreign keys (topic_id/post_id) are plain integers with no FK constraints or indexes, leaving orphaned embed rows that crash TopicEmbed.import with NoMethodError when the post is deleted, stalling the PollFeed job

adjudication.rationale: The diff creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` as plain integers and only adds a unique index on `embed_url` (no FK constraints and no indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id`). In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is found it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally uses it (`PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!`) if the content changed. If the associated post has been deleted (which the DB will allow without FK constraints, and no dependent-destroy behavior is shown here), `embed.post` will be `nil` and this path will raise (e.g., `PostRevisor` operating on `nil`), causing the caller job (e.g., `PollFeed`) to error out. The perf/index part is less critical, but the orphan->crash path is a real correctness risk in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: posts.cook_method default of 1 relies on the implicit Enum convention that :regular starts at 1; reordering the Enum would silently make all posts raw HTML, an implicit numeric contract between migration and Enum

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an integer `cook_method` column with `default: 1` and defines `Post.cook_methods` as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which does create a numeric coupling between stored DB values and the Enum ordering. However, the proposed finding claims a concrete failure mode ("relies on implicit convention that :regular starts at 1" and "reordering would silently make all posts raw HTML") that cannot be verified from this diff alone because the `Enum` implementation (whether it starts at 0 or 1, whether it’s stable/explicit) is not shown. The “reordering” concern is also hypothetical/future-facing rather than a demonstrable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cosmetic whitespace-only edits to the already-applied migrate_word_counts migration cause checksum/schema-diff noise in drift-detection tooling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include whitespace-only changes to `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` (removal of trailing spaces and a missing/added newline at EOF). However, this does not change migration behavior, and Rails itself does not use migration file checksums for schema state tracking. The claimed impact on “checksum/schema-diff drift-detection tooling” is tooling-dependent and not a verifiable defect introduced by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed job calls i.content.scrub but SimpleRSS only maps content on Atom feeds; for plain RSS it's nil, raising NoMethodError per item and stalling the import
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` is present, but for many RSS (non-Atom) feeds `i.content` is nil, causing a NoMethodError/nil crash and breaking the import. Candidate identifies the same root cause, though it doesn't explicitly mention the `description` fallback fix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: PollFeed passes unfiltered RSS/Atom content HTML into TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html, which is rendered unsanitized via raw post.cooked

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a path where RSS/Atom HTML is stored and later rendered without sanitization. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes that to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` short-circuits the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline by returning `raw` directly. The embed view then renders the cooked content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output any HTML (including potentially `<script>` or event handlers) contained in the feed item. There is no filtering/whitelisting on the PollFeed content path (unlike `import_remote`, which uses Readability tag/attribute restrictions), so this is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped interpolation of request.referer into a JS string in a script tag in embed.html.erb layout allows injection via crafted Referer header
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same issue: the unescaped request.referer (Referer header) is interpolated into JavaScript within a script tag, enabling XSS via a crafted header value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method raw_html in Post#cook bypasses the entire post-cook safety pipeline including sanitization, filters, and onebox handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and the `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` hook entirely. New import paths set this mode for externally-sourced content (`TopicEmbed.import` uses `PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], skip_validations: true)`; `PollFeed` passes feed HTML into `TopicEmbed.import`). There is no sanitization step shown in these paths (and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`), so this bypass is a verifiable change that removes the normal cooking/safety pipeline for those posts and can allow unsafe HTML through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-based access control in EmbedController is trivially spoofable, allowing attackers to trigger retrieve_topic jobs and force scraping of arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable authorizes requests solely by checking `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The Referer header is client-controlled and can be trivially spoofed in non-browser requests, so an attacker can call `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a forged Referer matching the allowed host. When no embed exists, this enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...)`, which eventually calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` and `open(url)` to fetch content. TopicRetriever does restrict the URL host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so the abuse is limited to forcing fetches of arbitrary paths/URLs on that host, but the spoofability and ability to trigger scraping/jobs is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed polling job has no error handling and retry: false — a timeout, missing content, or nil link kills the job silently and the feed is never polled again, with one bad item aborting all subsequent items

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set and `poll_feed` performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` plus per-item processing (`i.content.scrub`) without any rescue. Network/parse errors from `open`/`SimpleRSS.parse` will raise and fail the job, and a single bad item (e.g., `i.content` being nil causing `NoMethodError` on `.scrub`) will abort the entire loop so subsequent items won’t be processed in that run. With `retry: false`, Sidekiq won’t retry that failed execution (though the scheduled job would still run again on the next recurrence).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic redis throttle (setnx followed by expire) in TopicRetriever can leave a retrieved:<url> key with no TTL, permanently locking out that embed URL

adjudication.rationale:
In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? implements throttling with two separate Redis calls:

```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
```

Because `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are not atomic together, a crash/process kill/network error after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs can leave `retrieved:<url>` set without a TTL. Since later checks only call `setnx` and return `true` when the key already exists, that URL could be permanently treated as "retrieved recently" (i.e., locked out) until the key is manually cleared. This is a real correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil-post/deleted-topic cascades: PostRevisor called with nil post raises NoMethodError, and stale topic_id from TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed causes TopicView failures with no cleanup path

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces TopicEmbed records that store topic_id/post_id without any foreign key constraints or existence checks. In TopicEmbed.import, when an embed already exists it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the SHA changed. If the referenced post has been deleted (or the post_id is otherwise stale), `embed.post` will be nil and PostRevisor will later call methods on `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...`), causing a NoMethodError. Similarly, EmbedController#best trusts `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` and calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without verifying the topic exists; a stale topic_id (deleted topic) can cause TopicView initialization/rendering to fail. There is no cleanup or fallback path in these cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side postMessage origin check uses indexOf substring match instead of prefix/URL-parse comparison, allowing spoofed origins to pass

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring check, not an exact origin comparison. As a result, messages from an origin that merely appears within `discourseUrl` will be accepted, even if it is not the actual/expected origin for the embedded iframe. A stricter check would parse `discourseUrl` and compare `e.origin` to the parsed origin (or use a startsWith on the canonical origin). The finding accurately identifies this issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve synchronously polls the entire feed inside the request-driven RetrieveTopic job, coupling per-URL actions to a global expensive operation and risking sidekiq timeouts

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before attempting `fetch_http`. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` when an embed is missing, and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, so a per-URL retrieval job can end up polling the entire configured feed (looping over `rss.items` and importing each). This couples a single embed lookup to a potentially expensive global feed import and can make the `retrieve_topic` job run much longer than expected (increasing risk of long-running/timeout-prone jobs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb reload loop has no failure signal — failed RetrieveTopic jobs cause the browser to reload every 30 seconds forever, re-enqueuing jobs unboundedly

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it always does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) unconditionally reloads the page every 30s. If the embed never becomes available (e.g., RetrieveTopic keeps failing to fetch/import, or embeddable_host/embed_by_username misconfigured), the browser will reload indefinitely and each reload will enqueue another `:retrieve_topic` job. While TopicRetriever has a 60s redis throttle on *retrieval*, there is no throttle on job enqueuing in the controller, so the queue can grow without bound under repeated reloads/clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer passed as postMessage targetOrigin includes full URL with path, and null/empty Referer causes postMessage to be silently dropped so the embed never resizes
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using the full referrer URL (including path) as postMessage targetOrigin is incorrect and results in the message being dropped, preventing the embed from resizing. The candidate adds an extra note about null/empty Referer, but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS import path never applies the whitelist used in import_remote, and javascript: URLs in href are not filtered, allowing javascript: links to survive rendering

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The RSS/Atom import code path in `Jobs::PollFeed` takes `i.content` from the feed and passes it directly into `TopicEmbed.import` without using the `Readability::Document` whitelist that `import_remote` applies. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites `href`/`src` values that start with '/', and does not strip or validate schemes, so an `<a href="javascript:...">` from the feed would remain intact and be rendered (e.g. `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`).
